query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Microalloying an equiatomic FeCoNiMn high-entropy alloy with 1 at.% boron and annealing at 800 °C for 24 h produces a nanocrystalline grain structure (~50 nm) with B-rich intergranular films that pin domain walls, raising the coercive field (H_c) from ~10 Oe (baseline) to ≥60 Oe at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: equiatomic FeCoNiMn HEA (single-phase fcc), cast by arc melting, homogenized, grain size ~5 µm, H_c ~10 Oe at RT
generation.intervention: add 1 at.% B to the equiatomic FeCoNiMn composition and anneal at 800 °C for 24 h under Ar
generation.conditions: synthesis by arc melting, homogenization at 1200 °C, followed by annealing at 800 °C for 24 h in inert atmosphere; measurement at room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: nanocrystalline grains (~50 nm) and boron-rich amorphous intergranular films
generation.mechanism: increased grain-boundary area and B-rich films act as strong pinning centers for magnetic domain walls, elevating the coercivity
generation.predicted_outcome: H_c ≥ 60 Oe (i.e. ≥50 Oe increase) relative to the undoped baseline under identical treatment
generation.baseline: undoped equiatomic FeCoNiMn HEA after the same anneal (H_c ~10 Oe at RT)
generation.boundary: applies for B doping between 0.5–2 at.% and annealing temperatures of 700–900 °C in fcc FeCoNi-based HEAs; may not hold outside these composition or heat-treatment windows
generation.uncertainty: moderate; the thermodynamics of B segregation in multi-principal-element lattices and the reproducibility of nanocrystallization are not fully established

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two arc-melted batches of equiatomic FeCoNiMn—one with 1 at.% B, one without. Homogenize at 1200 °C, anneal both at 800 °C for 24 h in Ar. Characterize microstructure (TEM/EDS) and measure M–H loops with VSM at RT.
measurements: presence and composition of intergranular films via EDS in TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the B-doped sample does not exhibit an H_c at least 50 Oe greater than the undoped baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
